ov: A family of 128 species of glossy, often iridescent birds, famous for mimicry and for murmurations: huge flocks that twist and turn together. The common starling was introduced to North America, Australia and elsewhere, where it is invasive.
rg: Native to Europe, Asia, Africa, northern Australia and Pacific islands; introduced to North America, New Zealand, South Africa and more.
df: Insects and other invertebrates, plus seeds and fruit.
fx: A wild starling has been seen to copy a sound it heard only once.
Winter roosts of up to 1.5 million common starlings form in city centres.
